_what: The words and the channels that say an upload is a talk *about* the work - a news wrap-up, a press interview, an opinion piece - rather than footage of it. The shape rules (a title that names no work, a title made of hashtags, a title that claims 'official' on a channel that is not) live in scripts/footage_sieve.py, because they are shapes and not words; the lists here grow batch to batch, which is config work.
_rule: An official channel is never sieved by any of this - the user's decision of 2026-09-20 (config/footage_origin.json `_rule`) holds here too: 'RENNICK S4 | QUILL S1 - Crossover Clip' (Prime Video Canada) was refused by the indexer for burned-in credits in 65 % of its shots, and no word in its title says so. That one is the frame judge's to catch, not this sieve's. CF-0924: `credit_phrases` is the one exception - read for every channel, official included, because a studio uploads all its films and 'official' never says which work a cut is of.
_discipline: Every pattern carries `seen_in` - a real upload out of a real pool, with the indexer's verdict on it. A word nobody can point at in the data does not go in. The whole set was measured on the 25 labelled candidates of tests/fixtures/footage_sieve_1541z.json (the batch of 2026-09-21T1541Z, plus two ids named by CF-0297/CF-0299): the table is in tasks/CF-0309-*.md, and tests/test_footage_sieve.py holds it to those numbers. The set is small - 9 good against 16 bad - so a rule is in here for its mechanism, never for its count.

news_markers.what: what an item of a news round-up ends with
news_markers.why: a channel's weekly wrap names each work it touches and what happened to it; three such items in one title is a news programme, and the shots under it are other people's trailers

seen_in.title: SILENT TIDE 2 UPDATE, CONTROL RESONANT REVIEWS, NIGHTWATCH KNIGHTFALL 2 TRAILER, HELLDIVERS MOVIE NEWS

opinion_words.why: the title of an argument about the work, not the label of a cut of it. 'Why' is in and 'how' is deliberately out: 'How They Shot It' is the standard title of an honest making-of (measured: 'how' took 0 of 16 bad candidates and would have been a rule with no data behind it)

seen_in.title: In Silent Tide (2013) Why Brad Pitt's Smart Zombie Survival Rule Makes Total Sense
